cases.purpose: A live matching REPLY binds both domain names to the associative array and emits no stdout.
cases.oracle: RFC 8415 message and option layouts decoded by an independent Python codec over the datagrams a Python DHCPv6 peer received; the peer replies with values chosen by the fixture.
cases.comparison: Candidate dhcp6 in a mapped user namespace on a veth pair; an independent Python DHCPv6 peer in a second network namespace answers on veth1. Each failing assertion prints one line; the summary line must report failed=0.

files.case.sh:
IP=/usr/bin/ip
PY=/usr/bin/python3
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-dhcp6.py
die() { echo "SETUP-FAILED $*"; exit 90; }
/usr/bin/mount -t sysfs sysfs /sys || die sysfs
$IP link set lo up || die lo
$IP link add veth0 address 02:00:00:00:0a:01 type veth peer name veth1 address 02:00:00:00:0a:02 || die veth
exec 7<>sync.fifo
W2_SERVER_PORT=547 "$PY" "$H" server info sync.fifo 2> peer.err &
peer=$!
read -t 20 -u 7 line || die peer-pid
[[ $line == "pid=$peer" ]] || die "peer-pid-$line"
$IP link set veth1 netns "$peer" || die move
read -t 20 -u 7 line || die peer-ready
[[ $line == ready ]] || die "peer-$line"
$IP link set veth0 addrgenmode none || die agm
$IP addr add fe80::a01/64 dev veth0 nodad || die addr
$IP link set veth0 up || die up
settle() { read -t "$1" -u 7 line; }
for i in {1..100}; do $IP -6 route show table local dev veth0 > routes.txt; [[ $(< routes.txt) == *ff00::/8* ]] && break; settle 0.05; done
[[ $(< routes.txt) == *ff00::/8* ]] || die multicast-route
settle() { read -t "$1" -u 7 line; }
declare -A R
dhcp6 inforequest -i veth0 -w 2 -V R > out.txt 2> err.txt; rc=$?
echo "inforequest-rc=$rc"
echo "stdout=[$(< out.txt)]"
for k in "${!R[@]}"; do echo "$k=${R[$k]}"; done > bind.txt
settle 0.3
kill "$peer"; wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null
"$PY" "$H" verify inforequest-domains bind.txt

cases.stdout:
inforequest-rc=0
stdout=[]
verified inforequest-domains failed=0
case-status=0

cases.purpose: Decode multiple domain names and escaped label bytes; reject truncated labels, missing terminators, and compression pointers.
cases.comparison: Candidate parser with literal DHCPv6 REPLY hex and explicit expected output.
cases.oracle: Option 24 is a sequence of uncompressed DNS label sequences; the fixture checks safe comma-separated presentation and malformed encodings.
cases.script:
declare -A R
dhcp6 parse 0701020300180017076c61622d6f6e65047465737400076578616d706c6500 -V R >out 2>err || exit 1
[[ ! -s out && ! -s err && ${R[domains]} == 'lab-one.test,example' ]] || exit 2
dhcp6 parse 070102030018000402612c00 -V R >out 2>err || exit 3
[[ ${R[domains]} == 'a\044' ]] || exit 4
for packet in 070102030018000403616200 0701020300180002c000 07010203001800020161; do
  dhcp6 parse "$packet" >out 2>err && exit 5
  [[ ! -s out && -s err ]] || exit 6
done
printf 'domain-decode=ok\n'
